item.title: Saipan International School to host Inaugural Christmas market
item.description: Celebrating creativity, community, and holiday spirit (SIS) – With Christmas in the Marianas not taking place this year, Saipan International School has organized its inaugural Christmas Market as a substitute fundraiser for the school’s art department. The long-running Christmas in the Marianas community event has traditionally provided essential support for SIS’s arts programs while offering students a space to share their musical and artistic talents. item.title: Turn breadfruit into baking flour at an upcoming workshop with UOG Land Grant
item.description: (PR) – The University of Guam Land Grant Extension Service will host another session of its popular Breadfruit Flour Workshop from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. on Saturday, Dec. 13. The workshop costs $15 and is open to anyone interested in learning how to make their own flour and create healthy, homemade products using a versatile and nutritious ingredient. item.title: Governor lauds donation of new Marpi signs
item.description: (Office of the Governor) — Governor David M. Apatang, on Friday, Dec. 5, recognized SuperTECH owner Mar Masilungan for donating several newly installed signs at various tourist and historical sites in Marpi. The signs are now located at Banzai Cliff, the Public Cemetery, Suicide Cliff, the Grotto, and Bird Island. item.title: Congress weighs NMI for military, Coast Guard ship repair hub
item.description: THE U.S. Congress conference committee last week agreed to consider the CNMI as a location for repair and maintenance of military vessels and Coast Guard operations. On Dec. 7, 2025, the conference committee issued the text of House amendments to the Senate version of the draft National Defense Authorization Act of 2026, which includes two major provisions for the CNMI, U.S. Congresswoman Kimberlyn King-Hinds announced Monday. item.description: GOVERNOR David M. item.title: ‘Show compassion for Tinian patients’
item.description: REPRESENTATIVE Patrick H. San Nicolas on Friday called for compassion for Tinian patients seeking health services on Saipan. item.title: Trustee: Fiscal crisis strains NMI economy, Settlement Fund remains stable—for now
item.description: The Northern Mariana Islands continues to face severe economic and fiscal challenges as its tourism sector struggles to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic, according to a status report by Settlement Fund Trustee Joyce C.H. Tang.
